title: Current Professional Activities
text:
Within the Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science at Waterloo:

Since January 2025 I have been co-organizing (with Megan French) a Student Seminar Series designed to give grad students an opportunity to present their research. We also occasionally invite professors to introduce their work to a student audience.

If you are interested in giving a talk, please reach out!

In June 2025 I began a two-year term as a grad student co-representative (with Diribsa Bedada). We facilitate communication between students, faculty, and staff in the department and represent the student perspective at department meetings.

Beyond the department:

In May 2025 I began a one-year term as Waterloo’s representative in the CANSSI Student PhD and Research Network (SPARK) Group.

title: A bit more about me outside of academia …
Laura Bumbulis
text:
Welcome! I’m a second-year PhD Candidate in Statistics at the University of Waterloo, working under the supervision of Professor Richard Cook. I completed my BMath in 2022 and my MMath in Statistics in 2024, both also at the University of Waterloo.
My research interests involve multistate modelling under complex observation schemes as well as two-phase designs for failure time studies.

title: Teaching
text:
Credentials
Foundations for University Teaching in Statistics and Actuarial Science Certificate 



To earn this certificate, graduate students in the University of Waterloo’s Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science are required to attend at least six workshops (two run by the department and at least four run by the university’s Centre for Teaching Excellence) and complete two teaching practicums observed by a member of the department’s TA Program.   My first practicum involved running a 50-minute tutorial on random variable transformations (STAT 330, Fall 2024). My second practicum involved designing and running a 2-hour review session on finding and evaluating the efficiency of maximum likelihood, method of moments, and Bayesian estimators (STAT 450, Winter 2025). Both were observed by Professor Reza Ramezan.   More information about the certificate can be found here.
